foundations.summary: Validates immutable schema-4 source locks, canonicalizes per-operation execution descriptors with shared schema references, and deterministically renders the execution JSON consumed by the existing runtime.

request_response_shapes: canonical per-operation stream, write, operation, and command descriptors
optional database, changefeed, polling, rate-limit, and sync-transport execution objects
guarantees: all seven lanes are explicit
provider evidence is absent from the canonical runtime descriptor
rendering is deterministic
execution objects reject authoring-evidence fields

selection.notes: The schema-4 lock is the sole mutable authoring input; rendered JSON is the sole runtime input.

constraints: Unknown root fields fail decoding.
Lane state must match authored execution content.
Schema references must resolve to safe registry paths.
Runtime cannot read source.lock.json.
non_goals: Executing provider I/O.
Granting runtime capability from citations.
Providing a second runtime or diagnostic reader.

foundations.summary: Loads closed execution JSON bundles from the embedded definition filesystem, validates typed streams, writes, operations, CLI surfaces, transports, and database inputs, then composes declarative and registered native executors into one runtime registry.

guarantees: closed schema validation before registration
embedded immutable definition snapshot
declared batches can select only their source-backed allow-listed actions and methods
unrestricted upload media is available only through an explicit typed provider policy
one registry combines declarative connectors with sanctioned hook and native overlays

selection.notes: Bundle directory identity and closed execution fields select runtime contracts; source.lock.json is excluded from the embedded filesystem.

constraints: Unknown fields, duplicate identities, unsafe references, and invalid cross-file bindings fail bundle loading.
A declared batch cannot select arbitrary HTTP methods, paths, bodies, nested batches, or undeclared actions.
Provider-unrestricted media must be an explicit source-backed policy on a file part and cannot coexist with an allow-list or fixed content type.
Loading a definition does not prove its declared executor is implemented.
Runtime loads projected definitions, not provider source locks or this Atlas.
non_goals: Importing provider documentation.
Providing arbitrary code hooks from JSON.
Reading authoring evidence at runtime.

foundations.summary: Executes definition-bound direct reads, direct writes, binary downloads, and binary uploads through common preflight, request encoding, response handling, preview, approval, and command-binding paths. Its declarative base check can preserve an explicit exact allowed 2xx status set and an explicit response-byte cap through the existing requester policy.

source_forms: projected CLI command, operation, stream, and write definitions
request_response_shapes: action-backed named structured JSON record fields
closed provider batch envelopes over allow-listed named actions
declared JSON, form, and multipart writes
base check requests with optional exact accepted 2xx statuses and bounded response bytes
guarantees: declaration and input preflight before provider I/O
action-backed structured JSON is decoded only for declared record fields and validated against the write schema
declared batches derive every method, path, and body from an existing allow-listed typed action
interactive stream reads share one caller request budget across fan-out discovery, child sequences, retries, and redirects while saved ETL keeps its established unbounded zero value
one bounded provider-facing command invocation
preview and approval binding for mutation paths
declared base-check success statuses are normalized from unambiguous numeric spellings that resolve to 2xx and enforced as an exact allowed set when present
declared base-check max_bytes captures at most one excess byte and rejects oversized successful responses
response and payload bounds

selectors: CLI command binding kind and ID
write action name and request kind
selection.notes: The command runner resolves one exact declared binding and delegates to the common engine; unsupported or deferred bindings stop before provider I/O.

constraints: A direct command must remain bounded and must not own a warehouse checkpoint or saved sync lifecycle.
Structured JSON command flags are available only for action-backed direct writes, never as a generic operation body or HTTP escape hatch.
Declared batches cannot accept caller-authored methods, paths, raw bodies, query-bearing subrequests, nested batches, or undeclared actions.
Request fields, media types, response policies, and retry behavior must be declared and source-backed.
Provider-unrestricted upload media requires an explicit declaration and remains path-confined, byte-bounded, digest-bound, previewed, and approval-gated.
Binary upload uses typed write-action variants; binary download uses a declared successful response and byte bound.

A declared base-check success_statuses set contains unambiguous numeric spellings that normalize to exact 2xx codes and executes exact matches only; non-2xx values require the named exact response-status non-2xx execution gap, and response-status ranges/classes require the named exact response-status range execution gap. Omitted status metadata retains the legacy generic 2xx policy.
A declared base-check max_bytes is between 1 and the existing 64 MiB requester cap and uses that bounded requester path; omitted max_bytes retains the legacy response bound.
non_goals: Bulk ETL, warehouse materialization, scheduling, or flow orchestration.
Generic caller-authored HTTP requests.
Inventing provider retry safety or idempotency.

foundations.summary: Provides bounded hook, native-connector, and definition-factory seams for provider-specific authentication, request, record, protocol, and transport behavior without cloning the generic engines. Includes a definition-selected single_attempt destination seam: one declaration-bound request per record, automatic retries disabled, bounded response capture, and no provider replay or generic writer.

source_forms: projected definition plus registered implementation seam
sync_modes: definition-selected modes implemented by the registered native or transport factory
guarantees: explicit interface ownership
generated registration sets keep extension discovery deterministic
transport factories bind exact executor and mode references

selection.notes: Use the narrowest existing interface and keep the reusable behavior in its generic owner; definition-selected transport factories must not branch on connector name.

constraints: Extensions may implement provider-specific behavior only through a declared interface or exact executor reference.
A hook must not recreate common schema handling, pagination, request encoding, approval, warehouse, or transport orchestration.
JSON definitions cannot name arbitrary handlers or executable code paths.
Provider facts, mappings, and connector-specific executor selection stay in defs/<connector>; shared runtime owners must not branch on connector name.
non_goals: A general plugin or arbitrary hook system.
Connector-name switches inside shared runtime orchestration.
A second implementation of an existing generic foundation.

foundations.summary: Defines the closed sync-mode, checkpoint, tombstone, delivery, and executor-reference contracts and orchestrates definition-selected sources through a durable warehouse stage into definition-selected destinations. single_attempt is a constrained full_append/append delivery class: declaration-bound input fields, one request per record, automatic retries disabled, response-captured durable acknowledgement, and no automatic replay; retry_safe remains a separate keyed/read-back class.

guarantees: checkpoint commit only after durable downstream acknowledgement
closed executor and mode selection
provider source to warehouse to destination mediation
typed preflight before source or destination I/O

selectors: destination executor reference plus mode contract
source executor reference plus mode contract
sync mode and stream or action allowlist
selection.notes: App composition gathers only registered factories, then declarations select exact executor/evidence pairs; connector capability flags and names are not transport selectors.

constraints: A recognized sync mode is not executable until an exact source, destination, and mode intersection is registered.
Provider cursor, ordering, tombstone, idempotency, and scope semantics must remain source-cited and executor-enforced.
No connector-to-connector bypass may skip the warehouse stage.
non_goals: Inferring incremental semantics from hashes, timestamps, or external labels.
Allowing arbitrary lifecycle hooks in connector JSON.
Treating a declaration as proof that an executor exists.

Transport descriptor fields, executor-reference selection, factory registration, or orchestration order changes.
A supported source or destination role, guarantee, owner symbol, or proof test changes.

foundations.summary: Stages connection-owned source work durably, materializes WAL records into Parquet-backed DuckDB tables under declared apply strategies, reads back destination receipts, and executes saved ETL through the local warehouse boundary. Full-snapshot materialization does not require a provider row cursor; incremental and history strategies retain their closed durable checkpoint and row-cursor requirements.

source_forms: saved connector connection and stream definitions
request_response_shapes: recursive connector JSON strings including date- and timestamp-shaped values
guarantees: connection-owned warehouse paths
durable stage before destination apply
connector JSON string values retain string type through DuckDB and Parquet round trips
valid empty-object batches retain row cardinality through file-bound metadata and physical-schema checks
Parquet publication and destination read-back before checkpoint completion
typed dedupe and history materialization strategies
full_append and full_overwrite accept source snapshots without inventing a row cursor
incremental_append retains its durable source checkpoint and dedupe history retains its declared row cursor

selectors: stream primary key, cursor, and selected sync mode
selection.notes: Saved ETL resolves one source connection and the local warehouse destination; apply strategy comes from the closed mode and destination descriptor.

constraints: DuckDB is the only local query engine and Parquet implementation.
Empty-object reconstruction requires matching file metadata and physical schema; a sentinel column name alone is not authority.
Warehouse normalization must preserve JSON scalar types and propagate downstream emitter failures.
Every table and stage path is connection-owned and structurally validated.
full_append and full_overwrite are local execution policies selected by the connection; they do not assert a provider cursor, ordering, delete, or idempotency semantic.
Incremental modes still require an admitted provider cursor or event executor; warehouse materialization cannot manufacture one.
Dedupe history requires a declared row cursor; incremental append requires a durable candidate checkpoint.
Change capture requires its typed source and transport path and is not implied by ordinary materialization.
non_goals: A Postgres warehouse or generic SQL destination.
A direct API-to-API transport.
Using content hashes as provider cursors or primary keys.

foundations.summary: Reads pinned DuckDB warehouse rows, maps them into typed destination actions, persists a payload-bound plan and preview, consumes approval atomically, and dispatches bounded connector writes with result accounting.

source_forms: DuckDB warehouse tables and saved destination definitions
request_response_shapes: connector command plans for one bounded mutation
preview digests and single-use approval grants
guarantees: approved source rows and payloads are hash-bound before execution
approval consumption is atomic and non-replayable
destructive writes require persisted preview and confirmation
source table ownership is pinned at plan time

selectors: field mappings from warehouse columns to action fields
write action or connector command binding
selection.notes: Bulk reverse ETL selects a batchable write action; single-command plans may execute non-batchable bounded actions through the same plan and approval lifecycle.

constraints: Reverse ETL always reads warehouse rows and never substitutes a live API source.
One warehouse row must map deterministically to one bounded request for bulk execution.
Provider retry safety, idempotency, and read-back behavior must be declared truthfully and cannot be inferred from local plan hashes.
non_goals: A generic HTTP write tool or API-to-API shortcut.
Unapproved or replayable destination mutation.
Treating all write actions as unattended managed destinations.

source_forms: named saved connections, warehouse tables, and authorization references
sync_modes: modes selected by the referenced saved connection
guarantees: action checkpoint only after provider acknowledgement and read-back receipt
dependency-ordered flow execution
non-overlapping and non-replaying schedule fire leases
schedules retain references rather than approval tokens

selectors: flow manifest step kind and dependency graph
named persisted flow reference in a schedule manifest
saved connection and durable authorization reference
selection.notes: Flows orchestrate already-saved warehouse-mediated operations; schedules repeat a named flow and do not select connector executors directly.

constraints: A flow action must use a durable authorization reference created by the plan, preview, and approval lifecycle.
Schedules cannot carry credentials, approval tokens, or new authorization scope.
Flows consume named saved connections and warehouse tables rather than creating API-to-API shortcuts.
non_goals: Connector-owned schedule or flow CLI intents.
Using a scheduler as write authorization.
Bypassing saved ETL or reverse ETL safety contracts.
